notes: Quote by Abdul Shafique, President, Vichur Industrial Estate Manufacturers Association.

finding: AIEMA president: owners not switching on machines before insurer survey; shortage of surveyors delayed loss estimates
source_quote: People don’t want to take chances by switching on the machines before it is surveyed by insurance companies,
notes: G Aravind, President AIEMA.

finding: All 206 firms resumed production since Wednesday 6 Dec (state data)

finding: Only 60 of 90 companies functioning as of 7 Dec

finding: 110 of 126 firms resumed as of 7 Dec

finding: 220 of 250 units functioning as of 7 Dec; water stagnation persisted in places
source_quote: All 92 and 22 units in Pillaipakkam, and Therovykandigai, were functioning normally, while it is 114/116 in Vallam Vadagal and 220/250 in Gummudipoondi, a major industrial area in Tiruvallur district.
notes: Source spells it Gummudipoondi. Same article: stagnation persists in Siruseri and Gummidipoondi.

finding: 878 of 960 allottees operating as of 7 Dec; roads inside parks damaged

finding: SIDCO estates still draining flood water on 7 Dec, in contrast to SIPCOT
source_quote: While SIPCOTs are up and running, the same is not the case with industrial estates run by Small Industries Development Corporation (SIDCO) in Ambattur (north phase), Thirumudivakkam, Tirumazhisai, and Kakalur are in a bad shape with efforts being taken to drain the flood water out from the premises.

entity: Padi and Ambattur auto-component estates (Wheels India, Sundaram Fasteners, Lucas-TVS)
finding: Padi component makers all under water; industry observer: couple of weeks to restart after water recedes
source_quote: Padi has six major automobile component manufacturers and all of them are under water. It will takes at least a couple of weeks for these companies to resume operations once water recedes and they get access to the units,

finding: TANSTIA: machine damage may take a year to overcome; AIE chairman: 3-4 weeks to restart machines

notes: K E Raghunathan, Chairman, Association of Indian Entrepreneurs. TANSTIA: "it might take a year's time for the owners to overcome the loss".

finding: Factories shut 4-5 Dec, resumed 6 Dec

notes: Hyundai part already established; Daimler/Renault-Nissan added. Partly attributed to state public holiday.

finding: Some TVS group plants in worst-hit areas still not open on 8 Dec (Reuters via DH)

notes: TVS stoppage already established; this adds the 4+ day duration. nse_symbol left blank because plants unnamed.

finding: TNPCB directions under Sec 33A Water Act: oil hotspot remediation, compensation, LDAR study; operations liable to be suspended if norms breached

finding: State technical team traced spill to CPCL premises; noted inadequate stormwater management

finding: TNPCB told NGT: CPCL liable to pay compensation and operations may be suspended if conditions not complied

finding: Minister: plant must remain shut till further orders

notes: Links Michaung to the 26 Dec leak. Penalty later stated as Rs 5.92 crore (DH 21 Feb 2024).
